title: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
gist: A JAMA Psychiatry study finds anorexia and bulimia incidence up 71% from 1990 to 2023, and clinicians warn rising GLP-1 use, including misuse via compound pharmacies and online sources, may worsen the trend.

insights.claim: A JAMA Psychiatry study estimates the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa rose 71% between 1990 and 2023, across 204 countries and territories.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Establishes a rising baseline of mental-health demand that healthcare systems and payers must absorb.

insights.claim: In 2023 an estimated 18.1 million people had anorexia or bulimia, costing about 3.83 million years of healthy life (DALYs), and the study team projects 21.8 million affected by 2050.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Projected growth implies rising long-term demand for eating-disorder treatment capacity.

insights.claim: True eating disorder prevalence is likely far higher than reported, because anorexia and bulimia are less than half of all eating disorders; one expert puts the real rate near three times the figure.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Published figures understate the addressable patient population and care need.
insights.quote: probably three times the rate that they’re reporting

insights.claim: Social media exposure to thin-ideal, dieting and 'thinspiration' content is a plausible driver of the rise, and algorithms feed more of it to users who already have eating disorders.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Platform recommendation systems carry regulatory and reputational risk over harmful content to vulnerable users.
insights.locator: Social media may have played a role

insights.claim: University of Melbourne researchers found TikTok users with eating disorders received 4343% more toxic eating disorder videos than users without, and many were fed over 1000 problematic videos per month.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Concrete algorithmic-harm evidence that could fuel litigation or regulation of social platforms.
insights.locator: When researchers at the University of Melbourne

insights.claim: Pandemic isolation appears to have contributed: US hospitalizations for eating disorders doubled between 2018 and 2020, per 2021 research.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Shows eating-disorder demand responds sharply to external shocks.

insights.claim: Clinicians report more numerous and more severe eating disorder cases, with onset as early as ages eight and nine, and one expert would not be surprised if cases at least doubled again since 2023.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Anecdotal signal of worsening demand; hard data after 2023 is still lacking.
insights.quote: This is the worst I’ve seen things

insights.claim: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are becoming more accessible: 15% of Americans had used one for weight loss per Gallup, new easier and more effective formulations are in development, and many buy versions from compound pharmacies or dubious online sources.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Broadening, partly unregulated access widens the population exposed to misuse risk and to label or safety scrutiny.

insights.claim: In a small study, 30% of people with eating disorders had used GLP-1 drugs and about 10% appeared to have misused them, a figure the researcher thinks is an underestimate.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Misuse in a vulnerable subgroup is a safety-narrative risk for GLP-1 makers.
insights.locator: In a small study published earlier this year

insights.claim: Clinicians fear GLP-1s will drive faster and more extreme weight loss in people with anorexia, leading patients to present at more advanced, hard-to-reverse stages.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Possible downstream healthcare cost and pressure for prescribing restrictions on GLP-1 makers.

insights.claim: New research and clinical guidelines recommend screening for eating disorders before prescribing GLP-1s, plus more patient education and monitoring of users.
insights.speaker: Jessica Hamzelou
insights.so_what: Screening requirements could add prescribing friction and compliance cost for GLP-1 providers.
insights.locator: Bulik contributed to a set of research and clinical guidelines
